messages.subject: <Q> data format 'NA" or zero
parts:
Hello,

I am a newcomer to Distance Sampling, posting from Japan.

The following ULR (page;1) states to express with 'NA' if observed but
not confirmed.

https://workshops.distancesampling.org/standrews-2019/adv/slides/Data_format_for_distance_sampling_workshops.pdf

However, when I import text data containing NA
I get an error message and it is forced to convert to 0.
Can I proceed with the analysis?

Or should I delete the lines that are forced to be converted to 0?
However, there is a concern that this may result in a decrease in
density....

---
Best
Yasuo Shimada
Japan Weather Association, Tokyo

messages.subject: {Disarmed} Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] <Q> data format 'NA" or zero
parts:
Yasuo

Welcome to the list.

You must include transects where no detections are made. The question is what values to give to distance from the transect in this case.  The answer can be seen in some of the data sets that are provided in the Distance R package.  The screenshot is taken from the "minke" dataset in the package.


You can see that transects 5 and 6 had no detections so the "distance" and "object" fields are NA.

You should also consult R help on reading external files that contain the "NA" string:

?read.table

parts:
Ah-ha Yasuo.

Indeed the story changes when using Distance for Windows with regard to transects without detections. The text string "NA" means nothing to Distance for Windows and generates the complaints you share in your screen capture.

The CSV file you import into Distance for Windows will have nothing in the distance field. Here is an example of a CSV file to import into Distance for Windows that ships with Distance for Windows 7.5. Look in the "Sample Projects" directory, which on my machine is located here
C:\Program Files (x86)\Distance 7\Sample Projects\Example1.txt

You will see that transect "Line 11" has no detections, so no distance and no group size. On that line there are simply two tab delimiters with no values in between:
